newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rice exporters eye new European markets.
newsitem.headline: Indian rice exporters eye new European markets.

text.p: Indian rice exporters are exploring Hungary and Poland as well and north Korea as potential markets once seasonal supplies from Vietnam begin tapering off, industry officials and traders said on Thursday.

"We are looking for new markets like North Korea because the demand from North Korea is large and the potential is huge," Anil Agarwal of Space Group, a leading Delhi foodgrains exporter, told Reuters.

"Hungary and Poland have also shown a lot of interest in Indian rice," he said, noting there would be a seasonal dropoff this month in Vietnam's supplies. "Then Indian rice exports have a good chance to pick up," he said.
Agarwal said about 50,000 tonnes of rice exports to North Korea were currently being negotiated.
Traders said Indian five percent broken non-Basmati rice was currently quoted at $300 per tonne FOB, 10 percent at $290, 15 percent at $250 and 25 percent at $235.
"India is competing very well with Thai and Pakistan rice. Even good quantities are going to Ukraine and Russia," Agarwal said.
Traders said India had signed contracts to export nearly one million tonnes of rice from the winter crop.
"India has contracted for around one million tonnes of rice exports from the new crop and are under execution," Agarwal said.
India harvests two rice crops, with the bulk from the winter crop. Sowing for the winter crop begins in July and the harvest starts in October.
Reports from Amman and Pakistan said Iraq was in the international market to buy a substantial quantity of rice, and Pakistan traders expected to sell about 50,000 tonnes of rice to Iraq.
Anil Adlakha, executive director of the All India Rice Exporters Association (AIREA), told Reuters his association had not received any inquiries from Iraq.

"However it is hoped that once the ban is lifted by the United Nations on the sale of Iraqi oil for buying medicine and food, probably then we will get some inquiries for rice exports from Iraq," Adlakha said.
Iraq will be allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil from mid-December, its first sales since sanctions were imposed by the United Nations after it invaded Kuwait in 1990.
About two thirds of the oil funds will be earmarked for food and aid purchases.
Agarwal said there were some inquiries from Iraq, but they were asking for 365 days credit which Indian exporters were not willing to give.
"There is good demand from Colombo," said Prem Garg, another leading Delhi foodgrains exporter. "We have also sold 30,000 tonnes of rice to Iran during the past three days."

Adlakha said 1.42 million tonnes of rice had already been shipped in the first six months of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March), out of which 1.2 million tonnes were of the non-Basmati variety and 220,000 tonnes Basmati.
India exported nearly 5.5 million tonnes of rice in 1995/96, emerging as the largest rice exporter after Thailand.
Industry officials expect rice exports to dip to around three million tonnes this year due to a decline in global demand and less competitive prices.
